data.narrative: The student built a 13-row failure mode analysis document, then actually broke the system three times - stopped the database, blocked it with a table lock, and flipped the primary read-only - documenting what really happened each time rather than guessing. The read-only primary drill surfaced a failure mode missing from their table (partial read/write split), which they then handled with a real 503 + statement_timeout fix and re-simulated to prove it worked.

dimension_scores.observation: Ran all failure drills against the live compose stack without destabilizing the container topology; the DB-injection approach (ALTER SYSTEM + reload) meant no rebuild needed for simulation.
dimension_scores.evidence: Read-only injection via `ALTER SYSTEM SET default_transaction_read_only = on` + `pg_reload_conf()` with no container changes; verified restore off + reload.

dimension_scores.observation: Kept the failure analysis attached to the real deploy artifact (compose stack on postgres/redis) so every simulation exercised the actual production path.
dimension_scores.evidence: Simulations ran against linkops-postgres/redis containers; final healthy state re-verified (redirect 302, /live 200, /ready 200).

dimension_scores.observation: Used the observability pillars built in Module 4 to diagnose each injected failure - structured logs with request_id carried the read-only and statement-timeout errors.
dimension_scores.evidence: Log lines: `database write rejected: primary unavailable or read-only (transient)` with error_type=ReadOnlySqlTransaction and request_id f39ef018; `canceling statement due to statement timeout` with request_id 644c72da.

dimension_scores.observation: Enumerated 13 failure modes (not just the obvious down cases), classified transient vs permanent, ranked by risk, and discovered a genuinely new mode - read-only primary - from the live BREAK drill.
dimension_scores.evidence: DNS surfaced from a live drill ('could not translate host name'); slow-DB proven more dangerous than down (14.7s hang vs 4s fast fail); new row added for read-only primary with probability/impact/handling.

dimension_scores.observation: Converted the top-risk unbounded hang into a bounded failure with statement_timeout=2000 and gave the read-only write path a safe 503 with Retry-After instead of a 500.
dimension_scores.evidence: Re-simulation: blocked query aborted in 2.1s (was indefinite); write returned 503 database_unavailable with Retry-After: 5 (was generic 500 with leaked SQL trace).

dimension_scores.observation: Produced a complete failure-mode-analysis.md with dependency inventory (timeout audit), 13-row failure table, three documented simulations with before/after tables, and the implemented fix.
dimension_scores.evidence: caw/upsk/proofs/failure-mode-analysis-m5.md includes Chunk 4 with re-simulation tables showing before vs after behavior for both the read-only and slow-DB fixes.

strengths: Actually broke the system three times and recorded what happened - stopping postgres revealed the DNS layer ('could not translate host name') that the table had missed.
Proved 'slow is more dangerous than down' empirically with a 14.7s hang from an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, then fixed it with statement_timeout=2000 and re-proved a 2.1s bounded failure.
Diagnosed the injected read-only primary (reads work, writes fail) from symptom to root cause, implemented a specific 503 handling, and re-simulated to verify before-and-after behavior.
data.recommendation: In Module 06 carry the 503/Retry-After decision into a real retry-with-backoff layer and a circuit breaker for the slow-DB path - the timeout is in place, but clients still see errors rather than a transparent degraded mode.

public_evidence.student_action: Authored a 13-row failure mode analysis with a dependency inventory timeout audit, transient/permanent classification, and three live simulation drills.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Postgres connect_timeout=5/pool_pre_ping, Redis socket_timeout=0.5 with graceful fallback, DNS with no control, filesystem with no rotation - 6 of 13 rows had no current handling.
public_evidence.proof: Document contains Chunk 3 Simulation 1 (db stop: /ready 503 in 8.0s, /r 500 in 4.0s) and Simulation 2 (lock: >15s hang, 14.7s observed).
public_evidence.ability: Systematic failure mode enumeration and prioritization.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Shows the discipline that turns 'hope it works' into a prioritized, testable list of failure behaviors - the core of senior production engineering.

public_evidence.student_action: Added statement_timeout=2000 to the Postgres engine and an InternalError exception handler returning 503 database_unavailable with Retry-After.
public_evidence.technical_detail: connect_args options now '-c timezone=UTC -c statement_timeout=2000'; handler logs error_type (ReadOnlySqlTransaction) with request_id and returns error envelope without stack traces.
public_evidence.proof: Re-simulation: read-only primary -> POST /links returns 503 {code:database_unavailable} + Retry-After: 5; slow DB -> QueryCanceled after 2.1s (was unbounded hang).
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Directly addresses the top production risk (pool-exhaustion cascade) and converts an ambiguous 500 into an actionable transient status.

public_evidence.artifact: Failure drills (DB stop, DB lock, read-only primary)
public_evidence.student_action: Simulated all three failures against the live stack and documented actual vs expected behavior, then restored and re-verified health.
public_evidence.technical_detail: docker stop/start linkops-postgres; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock via background psql; ALTER SYSTEM default_transaction_read_only toggle + reload.
public_evidence.proof: Statuses captured: 503/500 (down), >15s hang (slow), 500 then 503 (read-only write), all restored to 302/200/200.
public_evidence.ability: Failure injection and incident drill execution.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Proves the student tests their assumptions about failure behavior instead of guessing - the entire point of the module.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Chose fail_open default, refined per dependency: DB fail_closed (never fabricate redirects), cache/broker/rate-limit fail_open.
Classified connection-refused/lock/failover as transient (retry), missing-table/bad-creds as permanent (fail fast, never retry).
Proved empirically with lock drill: down fails fast/loud (4s 503/500), slow hangs silently (14.7s+, no timeout).
Added statement_timeout=2000; re-simulated lock -> 2.1s QueryCanceled bounded failure.

teaching_approaches.detail: Live failure injection drills with documented before/after
